memo.verdict: Neutral; park; conviction medium. ING Bank Slaski (ING-PL) is a quality compounder at a fair price with a legislated tax trough in the middle of it; the record rates the 'Investment Thesis' D on a modal total shareholder return of about 9.5 percent a year over three years (10.8 percent on the upper-modal path) against the framework's 20 percent bar, and parks the case on its return, not on its quality. The gate line does not apply: no D or F sits on management ('No mediocre management' B), business quality ('Business' B), predictability ('Transmission' B) or trackability ('Leading indicators' B). Conditions named for progressing: the price at about PLN 343 (24 percent below PLN 451.2) at an unchanged multiple; or PLN 373 if both re-rating conditions (the tax step-down delivered; the net interest margin holding at or above 2.95 percent through 2027) have been met and the stock has not moved; or the sell-side's buy share rising through 50 percent on an operating upgrade to net interest income rather than a tax one. Conditions named for a bearish view: the margin below 2.95 percent in any quarter, or a government proposal in any form to extend the 30 percent bank corporate income tax; either gives the multiple's downside (about a third to a fair trough) a trigger, and the drop-through case (cost of risk at 65 basis points plus a tax rate two points above the legislated path) would move the 'Investment Thesis' from D to F.
case: - The visible change is a tax, and it reverses on a timetable the market already models. The bank CIT rose from 19 to 30 percent for 2026, legislated to 26 percent in 2027 and 23 percent from 2028; reported EPS falls about 11 percent in 2026 to about PLN 31.8 and rebounds about 15 percent in 2027 and 12 percent in 2028 on consensus. The rebound is in law, so probable; it is already inside the 24-month-forward EPS the multiple is struck on, and the FY2028 consensus mean rose 18.1 percent over twelve months as it was modelled.

- Beneath the tax, the forces are of ordinary strength and net to a mild headwind (E 1, BB 1 at C). Headwinds: the policy rate (every 100 basis points of cuts compresses the margin about 17 basis points or costs PLN 130 to 160 million of annual net interest income; management expects no cuts in 2026 and about 50 basis points in 2027; Morgan Stanley models 25 basis points in April and July 2027 to 3.25 percent); the 30 percent CIT removing up to PLN 800 million of net income; the countercyclical buffer to 2 percent; consumer-credit rulings (Case C-744/24, PLN 12 million of interest in Q2 2026; PLN 19 million plus PLN 70 million of provisions; UOKiK PLN 58 million); state-bank corporate pricing (tender yields as low as 18 basis points; Pekao corporate loans +14 percent against ING +6 percent). Tailwinds: credit at 32 percent of GDP against 80 percent in the euro area; private credit +7.6 percent; mortgage agreements +50 percent to PLN 47.4 billion in the first four months of 2026; deposits over-supplied (Supply side B). Internal forces (RA 2 at C): standards improvement B, new products B (ING TFI with PLN 56 billion of assets, 12 percent share, 778,000 clients, PLN 50.5 million of fees in its first quarter; subscription accounts; factoring), acquisitions B (ING TFI for PLN 405 million, 32 basis points of capital, closed 24 April 2026), shareholder returns B (payout ceiling 50 to 75 percent); chief executive C (internal continuity), strategy C (the 2035 strategy rebases the return target down to about 19 percent), guidance raised D (no earnings guidance; targets moved down). The core-system migration to Thought Machine's Vault (over 30 percent of applications on cloud) is the largest internal action and is more risk than force.

- 'Financial Outputs' (E 2, BB 1 at C) turned up at the operating line and down at the reported line, and the sell-side trims. Key metrics B (income growth 4.9 percent 2024, 7.2 percent 2025, 11 percent Q2 2026; cost-to-income 41.0 percent; capital surplus), not A because the margin compresses. Sell-side upgrades D (Underweight mean, three Sells, buy share 14 percent, FY2026 and FY2027 cut 1.8 percent over three months; not F because targets +11 percent and FY2028 +9.0 percent over six months). Goldilocks growth C: six months F (FY2026 EPS about PLN 31.8 against PLN 35.59, -11 percent, entirely tax); eighteen months B (FY2027 about PLN 36.6, +15 percent, of which about 10 points are the CIT falling); three years C (about 9.4 to 10.5 percent a year from the FY2026 base; about 4 percent a year from FY2025 to FY2028; underlying pre-tax growth 6 to 8 percent). Staircase C: mostly legislated steps.
counter_case: - The strongest case against the verdict is the bull's, carried at full force at the head of the 'Investment Thesis' and again at the head of the 'Investment Setup' and the 'Investment Case'. The market is mis-reading a legislated tax trough as a structural earnings downshift. FY2026 EPS of PLN 31.7 is the floor and FY2028 of about PLN 41 is the run-rate; a 20 percent return-on-equity digital leader at 11x the 2028 figure is cheap against its ten-year median of 12.1x and 75th percentile of 13.1x; the fee pivot (investment products PLN 83 billion, +174 percent; ING TFI's PLN 56 billion compounding with inflows) and the hedge roll (Erste expects net interest income to be positively surprised by expiring loss-making swap positions; the Sector Digest calls the hedge roll "the best setup" in banks) make net interest income surprise positively through the 2027 cuts; consensus revenue growth of 5.2 percent in 2027 and 4.1 percent in 2028 is below what a bank growing volumes 9 percent with a hedge roll delivers; the cost of risk at 33 basis points reflects a book whose Stage 3 ratio has been stable at 3.8 to 3.9 percent for two years, not a holiday. So FY2028 EPS is PLN 43 to 44, not PLN 39.6, and on 13.1x the bull's three-year value is about PLN 764 including dividends of about PLN 85, 19.2 percent a year; the bull's own framing is 13x on about PLN 48 of 2031 earnings giving about 17 percent a year with dividends. Evidence for it: pre-tax profit +15 percent in H1 2026; total income +11 percent, pre-provision profit +14 percent and provisions -79 percent in Q2 2026; six quarters of net interest income growth through cuts; retail acquisition at a six-year high (101,000 in a quarter); the Jefferies view that digital leaders deliver superior operating leverage over time; a cohort that has just re-rated.

- What the record concedes: the tax reversal is contractual; the franchise is the best in Poland by return and cost; the ten-year median multiple is a legitimate anchor; net interest income is the line where consensus is most likely wrong, in the bull's direction; the ten-year 75th percentile is a real level the stock has traded at; the provisions normalisation is a judgement, not a fact.
triggers: - Progress at about PLN 343 (24 percent lower) at 11.0x; at PLN 373 if the tax step-down has been delivered and the margin has held at or above 2.95 percent and the stock has not moved; or if the sell-side's buy share rises through 50 percent on an operating upgrade to net interest income rather than a tax one.

- Bearish view if the net interest margin breaks 2.95 percent in any quarter, or if a tax extension is proposed in any form (that moves FY2028 EPS from about PLN 39.6 to about PLN 36 and the case from D to F); the drop-through case (cost of risk 65 basis points, tax two points higher) gives 6.5 percent a year, an F.

- Margin: Alarm below 2.95 percent in any quarter, a cutting cycle of more than 75 basis points, or the average deposit rate rising in a quarter in which the policy rate did not fall; Invalidate below 2.80 percent, or deposit cost rising while the NBP cuts. Modal 2.95 to 3.05 percent through 2027, net interest income +4 to 6 percent a year.

- Tax and the regulatory take: Alarm any government proposal to extend or re-raise the bank CIT, or a new credit-holiday scheme; Invalidate an extension legislated. Modal: about 31 percent effective in 2027, 29 to 30 percent in 2028.
- Loan volume growth: Alarm below 6 percent for two quarters; Invalidate below 4 percent for a year; modal 8 to 9 percent.
- Core-system migration: Alarm a public multi-hour transaction outage or a disclosed delay; Invalidate a regulatory sanction or a write-off of the programme.
